chunks: From him, from Al-Hasan, from Al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from Ali, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), from Abu Basir, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the slaughtered animal of the Jew, and he said: 'It is permissible.' I said: 'But if he mentions Al-Masih (the Messiah) [in the name of Allah]?' He said: 'Even if he mentions [Al-Masih], for indeed he only intends Allah [by it].'
ai.seo_question: Is the meat of Jews considered halal if they mention other names during slaughter?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Istibsar*, Imam Al-Sadiq (AS) establishes the permissibility of Jewish slaughter even when 'Al-Masih' is invoked, interpreting the term as referring to Allah rather than a distinct deity, thereby aligning with the Shia principle of *istishab* (presumption of continuity) regarding the People of the Book. This ruling underscores the theological nuance in Shia jurisprudence where the specific name invoked is less critical than the intent of monotheism, distinguishing it from stricter interpretations that might require the explicit mention of 'Allah'.
